summary: Monkey Island entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: The Secret of Monkey Island
entries.definitive_edition: The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition on PC

emulation.notes: Use native Special Edition for primary; ScummVM only for original-release preservation.

primary.version: The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition
primary.why: The Special Edition is the current official route with remade art/audio, voice acting, hint support, and a switch back to the original presentation. That makes it the best one-route blend of access, fidelity, and historical comparison.
primary.how_to_play: Use the PC Special Edition through Steam/GOG where available. Record storefront/build, classic-versus-special visuals, hint use, voice/audio settings, and whether original SCUMM/CD versions were compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original SCUMM-era presentation and interface variants
secondary.what_to_play: Use only if preserving exact original look/interface differences.
secondary.why: The Special Edition can toggle original audiovisuals but is still a later wrapper/remake.

entries.title: Tales of Monkey Island

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Complete PC season with episode/build state documented

primary.version: Current Steam/GOG PC release where owned/available
primary.why: Tales is the episodic Telltale Monkey Island entry and PC is the cleanest capture route for all five chapters. WiiWare and older iOS routes are defunct or impractical, while current PC storefront/owned-library availability should be verified before capture.
primary.how_to_play: Use the complete PC season. Record storefront/source, episode, build, save/cross-episode state, graphics/input settings, subtitles, controller/mouse mode, and whether Wii/PS3/iOS routes were excluded.

secondary.why: PC is the practical complete archive route.

all_releases.reason: primary: best capture and all-episode route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Episode ownership/source and retired platform storefronts affect accessibility.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record episode/save state and storefront ownership; do not merge with LucasArts-developed Monkey Island entries.

entries.title: Escape from Monkey Island
entries.definitive_edition: PC v1.1 with modern launcher/rendering fixes and imported PS2 enhancements

emulation.emulator: Native PC with Improved Launcher/dgVoodoo; DREAMM fallback; PCSX2 for PS2 comparison
emulation.notes: Use owned data, cap game speed, and import only the documented PS2 assets. DREAMM is the stability fallback if the native launcher fails.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High-resolution PC rendering with PS2-exclusive audio/dialogue/help assets integrated.

primary.version: Digital v1.1 with Improved Launcher/dgVoodoo and the documented PS2-content import
primary.why: The PC release has the best resolution and rendering ceiling, while the documented PS2-content import adds that version's higher-quality video audio, omitted dialogue lines, and Monkey Kombat help chart. That hybrid resolves the real fidelity-versus-completeness split.
primary.how_to_play: Use the GOG or Steam v1.1 data, install the modern replacement launcher and dgVoodoo for high-resolution output, cap the game to its intended speed, then follow the documented PS2-content import using an owned PS2 copy. Test the Jambalaya rowboat because excessive framerate makes it move extremely slowly.

secondary.exclusive_content: Higher-quality video audio, extra dialogue omitted from PC, and a Monkey Kombat help chart
secondary.what_to_play: If the hybrid import is not used, consult the help chart and capture the extra dialogue/video-audio differences on PS2; a full replay is unnecessary.
secondary.why: These are verified PS2 additions, but the console port has a lower rendering ceiling than the PC version.

all_releases.fidelity: Original high-resolution-capable PC release; current digital copies are already patched to v1.1.
all_releases.reason: primary: best graphical route and supports modern launcher/rendering fixes.
skip: obsolete platform route and no sourced content advantage over the PC/PS2 hybrid.

all_releases.fidelity: Slightly higher polygon count and less pre-rendered material, but lower overall output ceiling than modern PC rendering.
all_releases.reason: secondary: source for higher-quality video audio, extra dialogue, and Monkey Kombat help chart.

all_releases.platform: Windows PC digital release (GOG / Steam v1.1)
all_releases.fidelity: Current legal PC data with the final official patch already applied.
all_releases.reason: primary: easiest source for the high-fidelity PC route and modern fixes.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PC offers the strongest modern rendering route; PS2 adds higher-quality video audio, omitted dialogue, and a minigame help chart. Import the PS2 assets into the PC setup, or use PS2 only for those differences.

entries.remaster_caveats: There is no official remaster. Uncapped high framerates can slow the Jambalaya rowboat, and current ScummVM support remains less conservative than the documented native-PC or DREAMM routes. The PS2 version is not simply better: its extra content comes with a lower rendering ceiling.
